STUDY DATE: Mar 08, 2019
EXAM DESCRIPTION:
MR UPPER EXT WO CONTRAST SHOULDER RIGHT
HISTORY:
Anterolateral shoulder pain for approximately 1 year of gradual on set and
increase.
COMPARISON:
X-ray January 14, 2018.
TECHNIQUE:
Coronal oblique, sagittal oblique on axial imaging.
FINDINGS:
Minimal if any acromioclavicular joint degenerative changes. Joint
undersurface does not significantly deform supraspinatus myotendinous
junction. Preserved subacromial space. Supraspinatus tendon ventral
insertional 1.0 cm thin linear calcific tendinitis focus corresponds with
x-ray findings on coronal oblique image 10 in sagittal oblique images 7-8.
Supraspinatus tendon is otherwise intact. Intact infraspinatus,
subscapularis, teres minor, biceps tendons.
Joint fluid is within normal limits. Trace reactive fluid within
subacromial subdeltoid bursa. Nonspecific trace hyperintensity at
posterior aspect superior labral base likely degeneration on coronal
oblique images 13-15. Other labra and glenohumeral ligaments appear
intact, as visualized. No significant glenohumeral bone marrow lesion or
hyaline cartilage defect. Normal sized axillary lymph nodes; no axillary
mass, paralabral cyst or muscle strain/denervation.
IMPRESSION:
SUPRASPINATUS TENDON VENTRAL INSERTIONAL SMALL LINEAR
CALCIFIC TENDINITIS
FOCUS CORRESPONDS WITH X-RAY. SUPRASPINATUS TENDON AND
OTHER MAJOR TENDONS
ARE OTHERWISE INTACT. SUPERIOR LABRAL DEGENERATION.
